summary.headline: Karnataka Bank Q4 FY26 PAT rose 40% QoQ to INR408.19 crore; FY26 PAT record INR1,310.50 crore, GNPA down to 2.78%.
summary.overview: Q4 FY26 showed sharp sequential improvement: NIM rose to 3.07% from 2.92%, cost-to-income fell to 50.47% from 58.72%, and GNPA fell 54 bps QoQ to 2.78%. Business reached INR192,118 crore with gross advances up 8% QoQ to INR83,340 crore, and CASA rose to 33.61%. Management said FY26 guidance was met on most metrics, but advances (INR83,340 crore vs INR84,000–85,000 crore guidance) fell short. Much of the Q4 earnings lift came from lower employee cost, higher fee and technical write-off recovery income, and accelerated provisioning, which analysts questioned on sustainability.

segments.name: Retail, Agri and MSME (RAM)
segments.commentary: RAM advances rose to INR51,197 crore from INR49,152 crore in Dec '25 (about +4% QoQ). Housing, agri, gold and vehicle loans added about INR1,547 crore to retail in Q4.

segments.name: Mid-corporate
segments.commentary: Mid-corporate advances grew about 13% QoQ in Q4 FY26.

segments.name: IBPC and food credit book
segments.commentary: Brought down to INR1,707 crore at 31 March 2026 from INR4,057 crore at 31 March 2025; about INR2,350 crore replaced in FY26 with higher-yielding loans.

segments.name: Deposits
segments.commentary: Aggregate deposits INR108,779 crore (+4% QoQ). Retail term deposits INR67,648 crore (+2% QoQ, +5% YoY). Bulk deposits fell to 4.2% of total deposits from 4.8%.

guidance_outlook: Business growth around 15%; deposit growth 10% to 15%; advances growth 15% to 20% for FY27.
CASA to be maintained at 33% plus; CD ratio around 80%.
ROA to remain 1% plus, with management saying improvement is expected.
Cost-to-income to be 52% to 53% going forward, from 50.47% in Q4 and 56.34% in FY26.
PCR to rise about 1% every quarter; Q4 rise was larger than that.
Management said NIM margin floor has been reached ("I feel it has bottomed out"), with ongoing focus on 3% plus NIM; NIM had fallen to as low as 2.72% in earlier data.
Business growth phasing: H1 about 39% and H2 about 61% of annual growth; management also cited a monthly target path.
ECL transition impact estimated at 1% to 1.5% of capital, spread over about 4 to 5 years (roughly 25 to 30 bps of credit cost per year).
Management targets recovering 50% of NPA and technical write-off books; called it ambitious and gave no figure.

FY27 product launches: tobacco agri input loans, programmable CBDC, NFC-based QR/Tap and Pay, surrogate-based housing lending, MSME dropline OD and LAP; major IT solutions due in FY27 include loan origination revamp, HRMS, treasury and BHIM 3.0.
capex_capacity: Around 31 branches opened in FY26; management said branch expansion plans may be revised in view of West Asia-related uncertainty.
Employee count fell in Q4 with about 350 to 400 retirements per month and no recruitment in Q4; some recruitment planned for IT and expansion.
Technical written-off portfolio about INR2,500 crore.
IT spending rising; major IT solutions planned for completion in FY27 include loan origination system revamp with collateral management, DevSecOps, HRMS revamp, Treasury revamp and BHIM 3.0.
demand_pricing: Advances fell from about INR78,000 crore to about INR71,000 crore in FY25 before recovering to INR83,340 crore in FY26; management said retail and mid-corporate growth is the focus and bulk advances will be reduced.
About INR2,000 crore of sanctioned loans were pending disbursal as of March 2026; management said disbursement began post April.
Loan repayments were about INR26,000 crore in FY26; management estimated total disbursements at about INR31,000 to 32,000 crore.
Around 60% to 65% of the book is EBLR linked to T-bill rates (about 55% per management figures), 2.31% EBLR linked to G-sec, MCLR 5.59%, base rate 0.31% at March 2026.
Management said EBLR is at its lowest and any upward move in market rates would help interest income; ALCO will respond as required.

qa_highlights.question: Why did advances rise sharply in the quarter and how does it fit funding and liquidity?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said CRAR was strong so it prioritised advances; funding came from available resources and some short-term borrowings, and funding was not a constraint.

qa_highlights.question: Guidance for FY27 across advances, ROA, credit cost, GNPA, NNPA and cost-to-income?
qa_highlights.answer: Business growth around 15%, deposits 10% to 15%, advances 15% to 20%, CASA 33%+, ROA 1%+, cost-to-income 52% to 53%. Credit cost was not given a number.

qa_highlights.question: Why did Q4 employee cost fall while other opex rose, and what is the run rate?
qa_highlights.answer: Management denied any one-time shift. Employee cost cannot be cut but was held down through staff utilisation; attrition of about 350 to 400 a month and selective recruitment for IT and expansion. No FY27 employee cost figure was given.

qa_highlights.question: Is other income driven by core fees or treasury?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said other income rose on fee income (processing charges, one-time ATM card fees, guarantee commission) and recovery from the technical write-off book; treasury gain about INR13 crore.

qa_highlights.question: Will yield pressure from growth squeeze margins in FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said EBLR is at its lowest and margins have bottomed; upward rate moves would help; ALCO will manage.

qa_highlights.question: Why were gross slippages so low in Q4 and what is the interest reversal impact?
qa_highlights.answer: Management credited SMA and CMA stress controls and recovery efforts; slippage was 0.20% in Q4 vs 0.47% in Q3. It did not quantify interest reversals.

qa_highlights.question: Will PCR keep rising, and what are the FY27 provisioning and technical write-off recovery expectations?
qa_highlights.answer: PCR is to rise about 1% a quarter; Q4 rose more. Recovery targets are ambitious (50% of NPA and technical write-off books) with no specific figure given.

qa_highlights.question: What is the G-sec versus EBLR book mix and the gratuity impact on employee cost?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said both figures would be shared later by email; the call gave only the rate-linked mix (EBLR linked to T-bill about 55%, G-sec 2.31%).

qa_highlights.question: What is the ECL impact on net worth and credit cost?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said ECL impact is about 1% to 1.5% of capital, spread over four to five years, with about 25 to 30 bps of credit cost each year.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Middle East deposit exposure?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Middle East and NRI deposits are a small share; the majority of deposits are domestic.

risks_watch: Sustainability of Q4 earnings lift: PAT jump was helped by lower employee cost (management did not give a FY27 employee cost figure or gratuity impact), higher fee income and technical write-off recoveries, and accelerated provisioning; track whether these recur in Q1 FY27.

Advances shortfall vs guidance: gross advances INR83,340 crore vs INR84,000-85,000 crore guidance; FY27 advances growth guidance of 15-20% depends on converting INR2,000 crore pending disbursal and on shifting mix from bulk/IBPC to retail and mid-corporate.
Margin path: management said NIM has bottomed and ALCO will respond to rate moves, but ~55% of book is T-bill linked EBLR and rate direction is market-driven; watch NIM vs the 3% plus target.

Slippage and recovery sustainability: Q4 slippage of 0.20% vs 0.47% in Q3 is well below prior run rate; the 50% NPA and technical write-off recovery target (technical write-off book ~INR2,500 crore) was called highly ambitious with no figure given.

Macro and external risks: West Asia conflict, energy prices and supply-chain pressure; branch expansion plans may be revised; ECL transition impact of 1-1.5% of capital, spread over 4-5 years (about 25-30 bps credit cost per year), not yet quantified in FY27 guidance.

Growth for the business is also target, there is a target for recovery also.
What quantum, what number, our aim is always to recover 50% of the book of NPA, 50% of the technical written-off.
I feel it has bottomed out. There may not be any chance it is coming down further.
We want to increase 1% every quarter. That number still I'm holding on.
summary.management_tone: Confident on delivery versus the FY26 guidance and on FY27 ratio targets, but cautious and evasive on forward numbers: no credit cost, employee cost, operating profit, or interest reversal figures were given, and several questions were deferred (gratuity impact and G-sec mix to be emailed). Management repeatedly described the outlook as measured and prudent given West Asia and macro uncertainty.

adds.what: Around 31 branches opened in FY26; FY27 branch expansion plans may be revised given West Asia uncertainty

growth.why: FY27 guidance of around 15% business growth, advances +15-20% and deposits +10-15%, backed partly by about INR2,000 crore of sanctioned loans pending disbursal and FY27 disbursement estimate of INR31,000-32,000 crore against about INR26,000 crore repayments, but no specific new capacity or contracted order numbers were given beyond branch openings that may be revised.
